text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zambian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Zambia Railways says it is negotiating with the Swedish International Development Agancy (SIDA) a contract to assemble a management team to restructure the company, which in recent days has been rocked by industrial unrest.
- Agriculture minister Edith Nawakwi says over $8 million released for the Rural Investment Fund by the International Development Agency (IDA) is lying idle because of bureacratic procedures.
- Visiting Malawi Bureau of Standards chief Austin Khumulula calls for a regional approach in the fight against cross border smuggling.
- Zambia's first firm to be privatised, Eagle Travel, is liquidated.
- Zambia Railways management orders striking workers to resume work or face disciplinary action.
- The law association calls on the police service to act against a growing crime wave in the country.
- The Mineworkers Union of Zambia and Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines (ZCCM) management fail to reach an agreement on new salaries and conditions of service.
- The United States gives Zambia over $7 million in project aid support.
